question: Why is using standard equipment for bariatric patients unsafe?

options.A: Standard equipment lacks wheels for smooth movement
options.B: Standard equipment may break under excess weight, causing injury
options.C: Standard equipment is usually too warm for the patient
options.D: Standard equipment takes up too much floor space

explanation: Standard devices have weight limits. Exceeding them can cause sudden equipment failure and lead to a nasty fall.

question: What does the reorder point represent in inventory management?

options.A: The cost of buying a single medical item
options.B: The date when a medication finally expires
options.C: The maximum number of items a shelf can hold
options.D: The specific stock level that triggers a new order

explanation: The reorder point is the threshold that tells the nurse or storekeeper it is time to buy more supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: What must a nurse do when they suspect an older adult is being abused at home?

options.A: Keep the information strictly confidential to protect family trust
options.B: Report the suspicion to the designated protective services authority
options.C: Wait until absolute proof is gathered before telling anyone else
options.D: Advise the patient to handle the situation independently

explanation: Nurses are mandatory reporters! You don't need absolute proof to report—just reasonable suspicion to keep your patient safe.

question: Which of these counts as skilled nursing care at home?

options.A: Purchasing groceries from the local market
options.B: Sweeping and cleaning the patient's bedroom
options.C: Cooking meals for the entire household
options.D: Changing a complex surgical wound dressing

explanation: Spot on! Skilled nursing involves clinical procedures like wound care that require professional nursing training.

question: Where should physical family planning client files be stored when not in active use?

options.A: Inside an open bin near the clinic entrance
options.B: In the public waiting area bookshelf
options.C: In a lockable cabinet or secure records room
options.D: On top of the consultation desk for easy access

explanation: Physical files containing sensitive health data must be locked away to prevent unauthorized access by casual visitors or staff. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h5)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Using private rooms
options.C: Taking daily antibiotics
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Spot on! Simple, regular handwashing is the absolute number one tool we have to keep germs from jumping from patient to patient.

question: Why is palliative care ideally introduced before the very final days of a degenerative illness?

options.A: To allow a smooth transition and build relationships with the care team
options.B: To guarantee that the patient will regain full physical mobility
options.C: To speed up the natural progression of the genetic disorder
options.D: To eliminate the need for any medications or nursing oversight

explanation: Early introduction helps patients and families process difficult decisions and builds trust with the palliative team before a crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h8)

question: Why should nurses encourage elderly residents to do parts of their own bath and hygiene care?

options.A: To preserve their dignity and functional independence
options.B: To lower the financial cost of facility operations
options.C: To eliminate the need for any assistive devices
options.D: To reduce the workload of the nursing staff completely

explanation: You got it! Doing things for themselves—even small tasks—helps residents keep their strength and feel good about their independence.

question: What is a major risk of using strong steroid creams on the skin for too long?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin to a deep black color
options.B: Skin thinning and atrophy at the application site
options.C: Complete numbness and loss of feeling in the treated limb
options.D: Rapid overgrowth of thick hair across the entire body

explanation: You got it! Overusing strong topical steroids can weaken the skin, making it thin, fragile, and prone to stretch marks.

question: What vital instruction must you give a patient who is taking prescribed corticosteroid therapy?

options.A: Double the dose whenever you feel stressed
options.B: Never stop taking the medication abruptly
options.C: Take the pills only once a month
options.D: Stop the drug immediately if you gain weight

explanation: You got it! Stopping steroids suddenly can shock the body because the adrenal glands go to sleep while on the medication. They must be tapered off slowly.

question: Why is keeping a narrow range for vital signs important for a patient?

options.A: It ensures the patient stays awake during the night
options.B: It guarantees that blood pressure never changes
options.C: It prevents vital organs from failing due to extreme stress
options.D: It stops the patient from needing any medication

explanation: Great thinking! Staying within a safe, normal range protects your patient's cells and organs from being overworked by extreme highs and lows.

question: Why is it important to know if a seizure was 'provoked' by a temporary issue rather than epilepsy?

options.A: Epilepsy is strictly a pediatric condition that resolves after puberty
options.B: Provoked seizures never involve loss of consciousness
options.C: Provoked seizures are caused by temporary triggers and may not need lifelong drugs
options.D: Epilepsy can only be diagnosed if the patient has had at least ten seizures

explanation: Spot on! If a seizure is caused by something fixable like low sodium or a high fever, treating the root cause stops the seizures without needing long-term medication.

question: Which skin layer acts as the main rate-limiting barrier to drug absorption?

options.A: Dermal blood vessels
options.B: Hypodermal tissue
options.C: Stratum corneum
options.D: Subcutaneous fat

explanation: The stratum corneum, found in the outermost epidermis layer, consists of tough dead cells that heavily restrict foreign substances and drugs from entering. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h2)

question: A breastfeeding mother who delivered six weeks ago asks for a contraceptive implant. What should you tell her?

options.A: She must first undergo a liver biopsy to prove her body can tolerate the progestin hormone
options.B: She is completely ineligible because implants will immediately dry up her breast milk supply
options.C: She is eligible, as progestin-only implants do not interfere with milk production and are safe during breastfeeding
options.D: She must wait until her baby is at least one year old before any hormonal method can be discussed

explanation: Great news for new mums! Progestin-only options are safe during breastfeeding and won't mess with her milk supply.

question: Why can a PET scan often detect diseases earlier than other imaging methods?

options.A: It uses a much higher radiation dose than standard diagnostic tests.
options.B: It spots abnormal chemical changes in cells before physical damage occurs.
options.C: It relies on the body's natural magnetic field rather than external machines.
options.D: It examines every single organ in the human body simultaneously.

explanation: Spot on! Cells change how they behave and use energy long before an organ shows visible damage on a regular X-ray or CT scan, letting PET catch problems early.

question: What is your main role as a nurse during family planning counseling?

options.A: To enforce government population targets
options.B: To convince every young person to get sterilized
options.C: To provide clear information so the client can choose freely
options.D: To choose the best contraceptive method for the client

explanation: Correct! As nurses, we guide and educate without forcing our personal choices on our patients.

question: Which surgical method allows a doctor to remove a uterine septum without making any cuts on the skin?

options.A: Abdominal laparotomy
options.B: Hysteroscopy
options.C: Vaginal colporrhaphy
options.D: Total hysterectomy

explanation: Brilliant! Hysteroscopy lets the surgeon work right inside the womb by passing tiny instruments through the vagina and cervix—no abdominal cuts needed!

question: A patient experiences a sudden seizure that immediately affects both sides of the brain with a total loss of consciousness. How is this classified?

options.A: Peripheral nerve spasm
options.B: Generalized onset seizure
options.C: Localized partial seizure
options.D: Focal aware seizure

explanation: When both brain hemispheres are engaged from the very beginning, the event is classified as a generalized onset seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is the main reason for doing screening spirometry on healthy workers who are at high risk?

options.A: To measure how much oxygen is floating in the blood
options.B: To cure existing chronic lung disease
options.C: To catch early breathing trouble before any symptoms show up
options.D: To find out which exact bacteria is causing an infection

explanation: Spirometry is a breathing test that can spot small changes in lung function long before a worker starts feeling short of breath.

question: Which group of hospitalized individuals faces the highest risk for severe falls?

options.A: Older adult patients
options.B: Visiting family members
options.C: Young pediatric infants
options.D: Night shift desk nurses

explanation: Aging bodies often experience muscle weakness, balance issues, and dizziness from medications, making older adults much more vulnerable to falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why is getting the family involved so important when helping a teen recover from digital addiction?

options.A: Household routines, communication styles, and boundaries heavily influence recovery
options.B: Parents are legally required to operate the patient's smartphone for them
options.C: It prevents the teenager from ever leaving the family home again
options.D: Family members are the only people allowed to prescribe counseling medication

explanation: Healing doesn't happen in a vacuum. Since home life shapes daily habits, the whole family working together makes a massive difference in recovery.

question: How does heavy alcohol use lead to a lack of thiamine?

options.A: By speeding up kidney filtration so the vitamin is quickly sweated out
options.B: By neutralizing stomach acid so that protein digestion stops entirely
options.C: By destroying stored body fat where the vitamin is primarily stored
options.D: By interfering with intestinal absorption and liver storage of the vitamin

explanation: Alcohol irritates the gut lining and stresses the liver, making it impossible for the body to properly take in and hold onto vitamin B1 from food.

question: How does making modern contraception easy for everyone to get help lower maternal death rates?

options.A: By shortening the normal physiological gestation period for women
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for emergency obstetric departments
options.C: By preventing all forms of sexually transmitted bacterial infections
options.D: By reducing the incidence of unintended pregnancies and unsafe abortions

explanation: Prevention is key! When people can easily access contraception, unplanned pregnancies drop, which means fewer people resort to dangerous, life-threatening unsafe abortions.

question: What is the main job of the epiglottis when you swallow food?

options.A: To produce sound through the vocal cords
options.B: To filter dust particles out of the nose
options.C: To warm and humidify incoming air
options.D: To cover the windpipe and prevent food from entering the lungs

explanation: Think of the epiglottis as a tiny trapdoor. When you swallow, it folds down over your windpipe so your food and drink safely slide down the esophagus instead of going into your lungs!

question: What is the main job of chemotherapy in cancer treatment?

options.A: To cool down inflamed skin tissues
options.B: To physically remove large solid tumors
options.C: To supply essential vitamins to the blood
options.D: To target and destroy rapidly dividing cells

explanation: You've got this! Chemotherapy drugs travel through the body specifically seeking out and killing cells that divide very quickly, which is what cancer cells love to do. Great job learning the basics!

question: What happens to sperm when they hang out in the epididymis?

options.A: To allow sperm to mature and gain swimming ability
options.B: To cool down the testes during physical exertion
options.C: To filter out abnormal sperm cells using white blood cells
options.D: To add fructose-rich fluid to the seminal mixture

explanation: Think of the epididymis as a training ground! Newly made sperm aren't ready to swim yet; they spend time here resting, maturing, and learning how to swim.

question: Which medical expert spends their day looking at tissue samples under a microscope to diagnose cancer?

options.A: Dietitian
options.B: Pathologist
options.C: Surgeon
options.D: Radiologist

explanation: Pathologists are the lab detectives who study cells and tissues to give us a clear diagnosis. Teamwork makes the dream work!

question: Why do we treat leprosy with a combination of drugs (MDT) instead of just one antibiotic?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any follow-up clinical evaluations
options.B: To prevent the bacterium from developing drug resistance
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing the medications
options.D: To speed up the immediate regeneration of damaged nerve fibers

explanation: Brilliant! Using multiple drugs stops the clever leprosy bacteria from learning how to fight off the treatment.

question: Which muscle group is primarily activated by the femoral nerve?

options.A: Quadriceps femoris
options.B: Gastrocnemius
options.C: Gluteus maximus
options.D: Hamstrings

explanation: The femoral nerve innervates the quadriceps muscles on the front of the thigh, which are responsible for straightening the knee. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h7)

question: Why is checking a patient's 'functional vision' so helpful when planning their daily nursing care?

options.A: It shows what the patient can actually see and do in daily life.
options.B: It determines the exact medical cause of the eye disease.
options.C: It changes the official hospital diagnosis code.
options.D: It proves whether the patient needs surgery immediately.

explanation: Brilliant! Functional vision looks at practical everyday abilities rather than just clinical numbers, helping us figure out the best ways to support their independence.

question: How do digital (electronic) blood pressure machines mainly measure your blood pressure?

options.A: By placing a small fluid tube inside the artery
options.B: By sensing pulse waves (oscillations) in the cuff
options.C: By feeling the pulse at the wrist directly
options.D: By listening to Korotkoff sounds with a tiny microphone

explanation: Digital machines look for tiny changes or oscillations in pressure caused by your pulse, rather than listening for sounds like we do with a stethoscope. Spot on!

question: Which bacterium causes General Paralysis of the Insane (GPI)?

options.A: Neisseria meningitidis
options.B: Treponema pallidum
options.C: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation: You got this! GPI is a serious neurological condition that happens when a syphilis infection caused by Treponema pallidum is left untreated for a long time.

question: A newly intubated patient has absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest and gurgling noises over the epigastrium when ventilated. What does this strongly suggest?

options.A: The ventilator settings are delivering too much volume
options.B: The tube is accidentally placed in the esophagus
options.C: The patient has a sudden blockage in the left bronchus
options.D: The endotracheal tube cuff has leaked completely

explanation: Gurgling over the stomach and lack of breath sounds on the left indicate the tube went down the esophagus instead of the trachea. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is the main goal of offering family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: To delay physical healing after pregnancy loss
options.B: To check for lower abdominal infections
options.C: To stop pregnancy from ever happening again
options.D: To help prevent rapid, unplanned repeat pregnancies

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps patients protect their bodies and avoid another unplanned pregnancy before they feel ready. You've got this!

question: Why is it important to interview a patient suspected of experiencing GBV alone, without family members present?

options.A: To comply with visiting hour restrictions set by hospital management
options.B: To prevent family members from asking questions about medical costs
options.C: To ensure the patient feels safe to speak honestly without fear of retaliation
options.D: To save time during busy hospital shift change periods

explanation: Abusive partners or controlling family members may intimidate the patient, preventing them from disclosing the truth if they remain in the room. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h7)

question: When should used items in the home visiting kit be restocked?

options.A: Immediately after returning to the health clinic
options.B: Just before walking into the next patient's house
options.C: Only when a supervisor inspects the bag
options.D: Once every three to six months

explanation: Restocking right after returning ensures the nurse is always prepared for sudden emergency calls without delays. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)

question: A client is discharged after an abortion without a birth control method and fails to return for her two-week checkup. What major risk does she face?

options.A: A permanent inability to ever produce estrogen again
options.B: An unintended repeat pregnancy due to early ovulation
options.C: Severe weight loss from sudden hormonal withdrawal
options.D: An automatic infection in the uterine lining

explanation: Missing the follow-up without a started method leaves a gap in protection during a time when fertility has already returned. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: What is the medical term for when a child starts going through puberty much earlier than normal?

options.A: Hypogonadism
options.B: Precocious puberty
options.C: Acromegaly
options.D: Delayed puberty

explanation: Great job! 'Precocious' means developing certain talents or traits earlier than expected—in this case, early puberty.

question: Why is respecting patient autonomy so crucial when caring for a GBV survivor?

options.A: Nurses lack the legal authority to administer medicine without a committee vote
options.B: International law prohibits nurses from offering counseling without a doctor
options.C: Patients always prefer that their family members make all medical choices
options.D: Survivors must retain control over their choices to prevent re-traumatization

explanation: Violence takes away a person's power and choice. Giving them back control over their care plan is a massive part of their emotional healing.

question: What simple inventory rule helps nurses make sure older ward medications are used before they expire?

options.A: Random batch sampling
options.B: Daily physical head count
options.C: Maximum-Minimum stock level
options.D: First-In, First-Out rule

explanation: Brilliant! The First-In, First-Out (FIFO) rule simply means the drugs that arrived first are the ones used first, preventing waste on the shelf.

question: What do we call a strange, unexpected drug reaction that happens because of a patient's unique genetics?

options.A: Therapeutic side effect
options.B: Anaphylactic shock
options.C: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.D: Cumulative toxicity

explanation: Idiosyncratic means it's a rare, one-of-a-kind reaction that catches everyone by surprise based on body chemistry.

question: What is the big plus of choosing a no-scalpel vasectomy over the older method?

options.A: It can be performed without any local anesthetic
options.B: It causes less bleeding and requires no skin stitches
options.C: It guarantees immediate sterility without a semen test
options.D: It makes surgical reversal much easier later on

explanation: Brilliant! The no-scalpel technique uses a tiny puncture instead of a cutting blade, which means less bleeding and a quicker recovery.

question: Which symptom should immediately alert a nurse to a possible ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Painful burning when passing urine
options.B: Itching and thick white vaginal discharge
options.C: One-sided lower belly pain and abnormal spotting
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Pelvic pain on just one side, combined with light bleeding during early pregnancy, is a classic warning sign we always watch out for. Excellent!

question: Which bacterium is responsible for the majority of bone infection cases?

options.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading pathogen isolated in almost all forms of osteomyelitis, whether acute or chronic. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h2)

question: A young girl who survived breast ironing displays intense social withdrawal and low self-esteem. What is the primary cause of these emotional issues?

options.A: Her inability to understand simple classroom instructions
options.B: Side effects from emergency medications given at the hospital
options.C: Distortion of her natural body image during puberty
options.D: A sudden chemical imbalance in her brain caused by fever

explanation: Unnatural changes and scarring to the chest during developmental years heavily damage self-perception and confidence. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the term for cancer cells spreading to distant parts of the body?

options.A: Metastasis
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Angiogenesis
options.D: Differentiation

explanation: Metastasis occurs when malignant cells break free, enter circulation or lymph channels, and establish secondary tumor sites far from the original growth. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h3)

question: What happens during drug distribution in the body?

options.A: The liver breaks down the medicine into waste products
options.B: The gut absorbs a swallowed pill
options.C: The drug moves from the blood into various body tissues
options.D: The kidneys eliminate active drug molecules

explanation: Think of distribution as the drug's journey out of the bloodstream and into the body tissues where it's actually needed to work! You've got this.

question: What is your very first nursing action when a patient starts having a tonic-clonic seizure in bed?

options.A: Restrain all four limbs tightly to prevent injury
options.B: Immediately sit the patient upright in a chair
options.C: Open the jaw and insert a padded tongue depressor
options.D: Protect the airway and turn the patient onto their side

explanation: Safety first! Turning them sideways keeps saliva and vomit from blocking their airway. Never force anything into a seizing patient's mouth.

question: What triggers the physical release of milk from the alveoli during breastfeeding?

options.A: Estrogen surge blocking milk ducts
options.B: Progesterone relaxing the nipple sphincter
options.C: Prolactin stopping milk flow temporarily
options.D: Oxytocin causing myoepithelial cell contraction

explanation: Suckling stimulates oxytocin release, which causes the tiny muscle cells around the milk glands to squeeze milk forward. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h1)

question: During shoulder dystocia, why should you NEVER forcefully pull on the baby's head?

options.A: It can cause permanent brachial plexus injury and nerve damage to the baby
options.B: It automatically causes the placenta to detach prematurely inside the uterus
options.C: It increases the mother's risk of severe perineal lacerations
options.D: It forces the umbilical cord to wrap tightly around the baby's neck

explanation: Pulling hard stretches and tears the baby's delicate neck and shoulder nerves, leading to long-term injury. Always use approved maneuvers instead of pulling!

question: Why do doctors order routine blood tests when checking for Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: To rule out reversible causes of memory loss like vitamin deficiencies
options.B: To measure the exact amount of beta-amyloid protein in the blood
options.C: To determine the precise stage of the cognitive decline
options.D: To check if the patient has a genetic immunity to brain disorders

explanation: Correct! Simple things like low vitamin B12 or thyroid issues can mimic dementia, so blood tests help catch treatable problems first. Smart thinking!

question: What is the main purpose of using screening tools like the Internet Addiction Test in nursing?

options.A: To diagnose underlying viral infections transmitted through the internet
options.B: To gather objective data on problematic technology use and its impact
options.C: To measure the exact electrical current flowing through the device battery
options.D: To permanently block harmful websites on the patient's mobile phone

explanation: Just like checking vital signs, screening tools help nurses measure how deeply technology is affecting a patient's life so we can offer the right help.

question: A new mother on her third day postpartum says her breasts are hard, warm, and very painful. What is likely going on?

options.A: A blocked lactiferous duct due to tight clothing
options.B: Physiological engorgement as milk production begins in large volumes
options.C: Acute mastitis caused by a bacterial infection from the infant's mouth
options.D: Absence of oxytocin release during feedings

explanation: This is standard postpartum breast engorgement! The sudden rush of milk, blood, and fluids can make the breasts feel very full and tender around day three.

question: What is the main goal of international treaties when it comes to harmful traditional practices?

options.A: To allow traditional practitioners to continue performing safe procedures
options.B: To provide financial grants directly to families who stop the practice
options.C: To place legal obligations on countries to pass laws ending these practices
options.D: To replace local court systems with international judges

explanation: Exactly! These treaties push participating governments to update their local laws so they can protect citizens from harmful customs.

question: What exactly is a vesicovaginal fistula (VVF)?

options.A: An abnormal opening between the bladder and the vagina
options.B: A blockage in the tube carrying urine from the kidney
options.C: A complete failure of the kidneys to produce urine
options.D: An infection of the lining inside the urinary bladder

explanation: You nailed it! A VVF creates an unwanted channel between these two organs, which is why urine leaks through continuously. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: Which device delivers a shock to stop dangerous, irregular heart rhythms?

options.A: An infusion pump
options.B: A suction machine
options.C: A cardiac monitor
options.D: A defibrillator

explanation: Exactly! The defibrillator sends a quick electrical current to reset a chaotic heart back into a steady rhythm. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: What is the main goal of creating a 'just culture' in the theatre workspace?

options.A: Making it safe to report mistakes openly without unfair abuse or fear
options.B: Firing any nurse who makes a small spelling error in the chart
options.C: Making sure the surgeon is the boss of every single nursing task
options.D: Throwing away all rules so everyone does as they please

explanation: A 'just culture' means we look at how the system failed rather than just blaming an individual, making it safe for everyone to speak up and learn from errors.

question: Why is getting an accurate diagnosis so important before treating any vaginal infection?

options.A: All vaginal infections automatically resolve on their own within forty-eight hours
options.B: Over-the-counter creams permanently damage normal vaginal tissue if used incorrectly
options.C: Treatments vary completely depending on whether the cause is bacterial, fungal, or parasitic
options.D: Providers cannot prescribe any medication without a blood test confirming the infection

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Antifungals cure yeast, antibiotics treat bacteria, and anti-parasitics handle trich. Using the wrong drug won't help our patient at all! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which government sector is mainly responsible for teaching health habits and running school hygiene programs?

options.A: Agriculture
options.B: Finance
options.C: Education
options.D: Public Works

explanation: Correct! Schools are our best platform for teaching children and youth healthy habits that last a lifetime.

question: Which complication involves facial swelling, neck vein bulging, and trouble breathing due to a blocked chest vein?

options.A: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
options.B: Superior Vena Cava Obstruction
options.C: Tumor Lysis Syndrome
options.D: Spinal Cord Compression

explanation: When a chest tumor presses on the big superior vena cava vein, blood gets backed up—leading to that classic puffy face and neck swelling.

question: What is the main reason a patient with acute pancreatitis is kept NPO (nothing by mouth)?

options.A: To rest the pancreas and stop the release of digestive enzymes
options.B: To prevent choking during sudden episodes of severe vomiting
options.C: To keep the bowel completely clean for diagnostic X-rays
options.D: To prepare the stomach for emergency surgical removal

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping the patient NPO means no food enters the gut, which gives the hardworking pancreas a well-deserved break so it stops producing damaging enzymes.

question: Why are bedside nurses considered the main line of defense against hospital complications?

options.A: They perform all diagnostic lab tests
options.B: They prescribe the preventative medications
options.C: They discharge patients independently
options.D: They spend the most time observing the patient

explanation: Spot on! Because you are right there at the bedside day in and day out, you notice those tiny, early changes long before anyone else does.

question: What must you ensure before sending an emergency obstetric patient on a long ambulance ride?

options.A: The patient has signed discharge papers against medical advice
options.B: All routine hospital laundry duties have been fully completed
options.C: A family member has paid the complete transport fare in cash
options.D: The patient is stabilized and secure intravenous access is established

explanation: Always make sure your patient is as stable as possible with a working IV line so you can give fluids or meds during transit.

question: What is the very first thing an occupational health nurse should do when an injury happens at work?

options.A: File a lawsuit against the company owner
options.B: Calculate financial compensation for the worker
options.C: Assess the injury and provide immediate first aid
options.D: Conduct a drug test on all witnesses

explanation: You got it! First things first: always check the victim and give prompt first aid or stabilization before worrying about anything else.

question: What is a major danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their long-term degenerative medications without talking to a doctor?

options.A: A sudden, severe return of symptoms or withdrawal
options.B: An immediate boost in liver and kidney function
options.C: Complete regeneration of normal nerve cells
options.D: An instant and permanent cure of the disease

explanation: You got it! Stopping chronic meds cold turkey can send the body into a severe rebound, making symptoms much worse than they were before. Tapering is usually needed!

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)
